note: Scanned / photoreal 3D models from Poly Haven (polyhaven.com/models), all CC0. Fetched as glTF with 1k textures by scripts/fetch-models.py into public/assets/models/_src/, then reduced to browser LODs by scripts/optimize-models.mjs into public/assets/models/<id>/. `period` is the span (historical years, no year 0) in which the object or plant is plausible in southern Britain; `confidence` says how good a stand-in it is. Budgets are upper limits in triangles per LOD for the category; an asset may override them with `budget`. Read docs/ASSETS.md before adopting.

assets.name: Gnarled broadleaf (coastal)
assets.plausibility: Species not stated by Poly Haven: a wind-sculpted coastal broadleaf with a gnarled trunk and small leaves. Not an oak or beech; at mid/far range it reads as a generic hedgerow or wood-edge tree (hawthorn, field maple, crab apple). Use as a stand-in only; keep away from close-up camera positions.

assets.name: Small twisted broadleaf
assets.plausibility: Species not stated; small twisted trunk with a spreading dense canopy. Reads as an old hawthorn or pollard at distance. Stand-in, not a named British species.

assets.name: Low windswept broadleaf
assets.plausibility: Species not stated; low windswept multi-trunk tree on exposed roots. Reads as scrub (blackthorn/hawthorn thicket) or a coppice stool at distance. Stand-in only.

assets.name: Slender young broadleaf
assets.plausibility: FLAGGED: Poly Haven tags it Burkea africana (an African savanna tree), not a British species. Kept as a slender-trunk, airy-canopy form that reads like a young birch or rowan at mid/far range. Do not use for close-ups; prefer the procedural trees where species matters.

assets.name: Pine sapling
assets.plausibility: Pine of unstated species; form fits Scots pine (Pinus sylvestris, native). Use SPARINGLY: Scots pine was largely gone from lowland southern England after the mid-Holocene and was replanted mostly after 1625; plausible on prehistoric heath and sandy commons only.

assets.name: Young pine
assets.plausibility: As pine_sapling_small: reads as a young Scots pine. Sparingly, prehistoric heathland only; not a London street or Thames-side tree in the historic periods.

assets.name: Leafy sapling shrub
assets.plausibility: Generic low shrub with narrow lanceolate leaves; reads like a willow or sallow sapling clump at range. Species not stated.

assets.name: Meadow herb with seed spikes
assets.plausibility: Generic meadow herb (paired oval leaves, upright seed spikes) that reads like a plantain or dock in a field margin. Species not stated.

assets.name: Glossy-leaved shrub sprigs
assets.plausibility: Glossy-leaved woody sprigs; reads as privet, box or young holly undergrowth. Species not stated.

assets.name: Fern clumps
assets.plausibility: Four fern clumps with serrated fronds; reads as male fern / lady fern (native woodland ferns). Good for wood floors and shaded banks.

assets.name: Stinging nettle
assets.plausibility: Stinging nettle (Urtica dioica), native and abundant on nitrogen-rich ground: middens, settlement edges, ditches. Excellent around any settlement in every period.

assets.name: Low weed clusters
assets.plausibility: Small glossy weeds with reddish stems (reads as knotgrass/dock seedlings on disturbed ground). Species not stated; fine as trampled-verge filler.

assets.name: Sorrel clumps
assets.plausibility: FLAGGED: Oxalis with pink flowers, probably not native wood sorrel (Oxalis acetosella has white, lilac-veined flowers). Use sparingly in shade; flowers are small enough to pass at range.

assets.name: Dandelion rosettes
assets.plausibility: Dandelion (Taraxacum officinale agg.), native; grassland, verges, trampled ground. Spring flowering.

assets.name: Lesser celandine
assets.plausibility: Lesser celandine (Ficaria verna), native; damp woodland floors, hedge banks, stream sides. Flowers Feb–May.

assets.name: Moss clump
assets.plausibility: Generic woodland moss clump; universal on damp stone, roots, thatch edges and north faces.

assets.name: Grass tuft (green)
assets.plausibility: Medium meadow grass tuft; generic temperate grassland, native-looking.

assets.name: Grass tuft (green-brown)
assets.plausibility: Medium grass tuft with brown strands; pasture, verge, grazed downland (Stonehenge, battlefields).

assets.name: Fallen log
assets.plausibility: Long weathered log with moss; species-neutral deadwood. Woods, field edges, timber yards.

assets.name: Dead trunk with stub
assets.plausibility: Decayed dry trunk with lichen and broken stub; species-neutral.

assets.name: Tree stump with roots
assets.plausibility: Decayed stump with exposed roots; species-neutral. Ideal for cleared woodland (Neolithic clearance onward) and felled timber.

assets.name: Mossy tree stump
assets.plausibility: Mossy stump with roots and leaf litter; species-neutral.

assets.name: Dry branches
assets.plausibility: Scanned dry branches; brushwood, kindling piles, hedge laying, wattle stock.

assets.name: Root cluster
assets.plausibility: Tangled exposed roots with forest-floor litter; eroded banks, river edges, holloways.

assets.name: Weathered boulder
assets.plausibility: Jagged lichen-covered boulder with rusty streaks. Generic field boulder; too angular for a sarsen but usable as a glacial erratic or quarry stone.

assets.name: Rock (earth tones)
assets.plausibility: Small erosion-worn rock; generic fieldstone.

assets.name: Small rock (rust-brown)
assets.plausibility: Small rust-brown stone; ironstone-like, plausible in Weald / Thames gravels.

assets.name: Quartz pebble stone
assets.plausibility: Reddish quartzy stone; reads as a Thames-gravel cobble or field clearance stone.

assets.name: Mossy rocks set A
assets.plausibility: Six mossy woodland stones; generic, useful as rubble, field clearance cairns, stream stones.

assets.name: Mossy rocks set B
assets.plausibility: Moss-covered stones set; generic.

assets.name: Sandstone boulders
assets.plausibility: Weathered Karoo sandstone (South Africa). Closest Poly Haven surface to a sarsen (a silcrete sandstone): rounded, layered, pitted. Tint towards grey (#b8b4a8) for Wiltshire sarsens / Marlborough Downs 'grey wethers'.

assets.name: Sandstone boulder (rounded)
assets.plausibility: As namaqualand_boulder_02; rounded sandstone boulder usable as an unworked sarsen on the downs. Tint grey.

assets.name: Oak cask (iron hoops)
assets.plausibility: Oak stave cask with iron hoops and bung. Coopered casks arrive with the Romans; before c.1600 most were bound with split hazel/willow hoops, so iron hoops are a late-period look. Fine for wharves and inns 1400–1625.

assets.name: Barrels and loose staves
assets.plausibility: Group of weathered casks with loose staves; same hoop caveat as wine_barrel_01. Wharf and cooperage dressing.

assets.name: Wooden bucket with bail
assets.plausibility: Stave bucket with metal bands and iron bail handle; medieval buckets are well attested (often withy-bound).

assets.name: Wide wooden tub
assets.plausibility: Wide coopered tub with two handles; washing/brewing tub. Same hoop caveat.

assets.name: Sea chest with rope handles
assets.plausibility: FLAGGED late: plank chest with rope handles, rivets and latch, a 16th–17th c. seaman's chest look. Tudor/Jacobean wharves only.

assets.name: Iron-bound chest
assets.plausibility: Wooden chest with iron straps and rivets; iron-bound coffers and parish chests are medieval. Avoid the open/gold staging, use closed.

assets.name: Carved wooden bowl
assets.plausibility: Hand-carved bowl; wooden treen bowls are the commonest medieval tableware and known from prehistory.

assets.name: Turned wooden bowl (burr)
assets.plausibility: Small turned burr-wood bowl; lathe-turned treen from the Iron Age onward.

assets.name: Lidded glazed jar
assets.plausibility: Hand-thrown lidded jar with twin handles and aged beige glaze; reads as medieval/post-medieval glazed earthenware storage jar.

assets.name: Turned-leg stool
assets.plausibility: Round-seated stool with turned legs; turned stools are attested in medieval and Tudor households.

assets.name: Rustic footstool
assets.plausibility: Crude handmade stool with tool marks; any period.

assets.name: Plain plank table
assets.plausibility: Simple four-legged plank table; varnish sheen is slightly modern, otherwise period-neutral.

assets.name: Stone hearth ring
assets.plausibility: Ring of soot-darkened boulders; an open hearth plausible in any period (camps, middens, outdoor cooking).

assets.name: Kite shield
assets.plausibility: Painted wooden kite shield with iron rim; Norman-era form (Bayeux Tapestry). 11th–13th c. only.

assets.name: Wood axe
assets.plausibility: Iron felling axe on a wooden haft; the metal butt cap is a modern touch invisible beyond a few metres.

assets.name: Arched iron-strapped door
assets.plausibility: Arched double door with iron straps, ring handles and small grilles; medieval gatehouse / church / hall door.

assets.name: Dutch merchant ship
assets.plausibility: FLAGGED late: a 17th-c. Dutch sailing ship. Plausible in the Pool of London only c.1590–1625; not a medieval cog or hulk. Too big for the props budget, hence its own category.

assets.name: Pinnace
assets.plausibility: FLAGGED late: a small late-16th/17th-c. pinnace with rigging and sails. Thames estuary / Pool of London c.1570–1625 only.
